ledgerReconciliation.purpose: Records, per environment, which local migration VERSIONS are already represented in that environment's applied ledger under a different version identity (renumber), split across several ledger rows (consolidation), or made unnecessary by other applied state (supersession). Without this, scripts/staging-deploy-preflight.mjs compares bare version strings and reports historical renumbering as deployment drift. This never renames, deletes, reorders or re-applies a migration: it only records an explicit, evidence-backed decision that a version difference is not a missing capability. Anything NOT listed here is still treated as genuinely pending and blocks the gate. Build 34 adds knownPending so an environment that is INTENTIONALLY behind (production) can truthfully say so: the old vocabulary could only express "already present or superseded", which forced a false reconciliation claim as the only way to make the gate pass. The gate model is now EXACTLY_ONE_EXPLICITLY_APPROVED_PENDING_MIGRATION + ZERO_UNEXPLAINED_DRIFT. Anything not declared in one of these sections is still unexplained drift and still fails closed.

Renumber claims are additionally corroborated by the production ledger row's own logical name and statement length, by the migration files' in-repo provenance headers, and in one case (20260723050000) by an exact normalised md5 match against the production ledger statements. Nothing was applied, recorded or changed: PRODUCTION_MUTATED=NO.
